Capture one single-display window without activating it and emit a coordinate contract (macOS and Linux). Linux uses an AT-SPI display crop.

Usage: auv invoke window.capture [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --title <TEXT>       Window title text used to select the capture target
      --target <TARGET>    Optional app:<bundle-id> (bare ids accepted); window and display targets are unsupported.
      --dry-run            Validate the operation without performing it.
      --no-overlay         Disable live visual overlay presentation.
      --store-root <PATH>  Directory used to persist the recorded run and artifacts.
      --json               Render machine-readable JSON output.
      --compact-json       Render single-line JSON with all result, verification, failure, and artifact fields preserved.
      --detail             Include diagnostic detail in human output.
      --wide               Include extra columns in human table output.
  -h, --help               Print help

Examples:
  auv invoke window.capture --title Untitled
  auv invoke window.capture --target com.apple.TextEdit --title Untitled

On Linux, app targets match the AT-SPI AccessibleId in window.list (BUNDLE in --wide output). Use --title when that field is absent. Linux captures a display crop and does not activate or unocclude the window.
